title: Starter SDKenV Microworkshop Manual
content:
Overview:
This is a compact, instructor-led microworkshop designed to get a small engineering team (1-3 devs) from zero -> instrumented sample app against Redwood in under 90 minutes. Focus is on pedagogy: low friction, observable wins, and clear fallbacks. Not a full course — a hands-on lab that results in a working prototype, minimal telemetry, and a short runbook for the next steps.

Goals (90-minute scope):
- Install and run the polyglot SDKenV (node + python snippets).
- Send first 10 requests and verify latency/cost telemetry.
- Add simple prefix caching + a KV-light warmup and measure effect.
- Create a two-prompt smoke-suite and detect one deliberate prompt regression.
- Capture a short incident checklist for triage and rollback.

Audience:
- Small product teams integrating Redwood APIs for the first time.
- Developer advocates running internal demos.

Pre-work (send to attendees 48h before):
- Confirm Redwood account + API key (or sandbox token).
- Install Node 18+, Python 3.11+, git, and Docker (optional).
- Clone workshop repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/microworkshop-starter.git
- Quickenv setup: cp .env.example .env and paste API_KEY.

Room setup and materials (instructor):
- Project repo with prewritten starter app and tests.
- Slide deck (5 slides) with flow and failure-mode cheats.
- Shared terminal (tmux or vscode live-share) for demo.
- Telemetry dashboard template URL and minimal query snippets.

Agenda (90 minutes):
0-10m: Kickoff + expectations. Explain scope and success criteria.
10-30m: Local install + run starter app. Instructor demo, then pair practice.
30-55m: Send first 10 requests; inspect logs and telemetry.
55-70m: Add a tiny cache + KV warmup; re-run and compare metrics.
70-85m: Prompt regression test (introduce a break, detect it, rollback).
85-90m: Wrap-up + next steps checklist.

Lab 1 — First Run (10-30m):
- Commands (Node):
  - npm install && npm run dev
  - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"Hello from workshop"}'
- Commands (Python):
  - pip install -r requirements.txt
  - python -m examples.quick_start
- Success: app returns well-formed JSON, request shows in telemetry within 10s.

Lab 2 — Telemetry and First-10-Requests (30-55m):
- What to capture: request_id, model, token_count, latency_ms, cost_estimate_usd, route (hosted/dedicated), dev_env tag.
- Minimal telemetry event names: "sdk.request.sent", "sdk.request.finish", "sdk.kv.warmup", "sdk.cache.hit".
- Example quick query (dashboard): average(latency_ms) for last 10 requests grouped by model.
- Exercise: run 10 scripted prompts (scripts/first10.sh) and paste dashboard screenshot into shared doc.

Lab 3 — Tiny Cache + KV Warmup (55-70m):
- Goal: demonstrate 20-50% token-cost reduction for repeated prefixes without hurting latency.
- Implementation sketch (single-file change):
  - Add memory-backed prefix cache (TTL 30s) around the HTTP client.
  - On cold start, run a small key-value warmup: call embed() for top-3 starter prompts and store KV.
- Measurement: run the first10 suite cold vs warm and capture token_count and cost_estimate_usd.

Lab 4 — Prompt Regression Smoke-Test (70-85m):
- Set up two golden prompts in tests/prompt_suites.yaml: one for factual recall, one for formatting output.
- Instructor introduces a deliberate prompt change in the app (e.g., drops role instruction).
- Run smoke tests; expected failure should appear.
- Rollback flow: git revert, re-run tests, re-deploy.

Quick Triage Playbook (85-90m):
- If requests 500: check error traces -> is it auth/key? Check header usage.
- If latency spikes: confirm region & route; check batch settings and concurrent KV misses.
- If quality regressions: run prompt smoke-suite to narrow down commit.
- If cost unexpectedly high: look at token_count distribution and new prompt templates.

Success Criteria (post-workshop):
- Team can run local app and send 10 requests.
- Simple telemetry dashboard populated with latency and cost metrics.
- One tiny cache & warmup added and measured.
- Prompt smoke-suite fails when expected and team knows rollback steps.

Artifacts included in repo: (instructor only)
- starter-app/ (node + python minimal wrappers)
- scripts/first10.sh, scripts/compare_metrics.py
- tests/prompt_suites.yaml (2 golden prompts)
- dashboards/telemetry-template.json (grafana/console snippet)
- README.md with quick links and troubleshooting notes

Failure modes & mitigations (short list):
- Broken env vars: provide a one-liner to dump env and spot empty API_KEY.
  mitigation: fallback to a sandbox token and pre-provisioned demo account.
- Local firewall blocking outbound: fallback to running inside a Docker container with host network.
- Non-deterministic outputs for tests: pin model to deterministic variant (sampling=0) for smoke suite.
- Long cold-start jitter: use a warmed dedicated route or run a warmup job as part of the lab.

Follow-up checklist for teams (post-workshop):
- Add the telemetry event names to the SDK instrumentation guide.
- Commit prompt_suites.yaml to repo as gating checks.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up to convert the experiment into an internal template.
- Optional: enable autoscaling policy template from dedicated plans if going to prod.

Instructor notes (things to call out):
- Keep the first run very simple: return a single sentence per prompt to avoid token explosion.
- Emphasize measurement over micro-optimizations; show graphs of token_count vs cost.
- Encourage attendees to write one quick bug triage card during the lab to practice rollback.
- Be ready with a pre-warmed demo if network or keys fail for >5 minutes.

Appendix (snippets):
- Node sample quick request:
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-small', input: prompt })
  });
- Python quick request:
  import requests
  r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {os.environ.get("API_KEY")}'}, json={'model':'redwood-small','input':prompt})

- Minimal cache pseudocode:
  cache_key = hash(prefix)
  if cache.has(cache_key): emit('sdk.cache.hit')
  else: emit('sdk.cache.miss'); resp = client.send(prefix); cache.set(cache_key, resp, ttl=30)

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally small and reproducible. Convert to a short slide deck and a recorded 15-minute demo after the first two runs.
